Rice cultivation: 1) Prepare nursery in May-June, 2) Transplant 25-30 day seedlings in flooded field, 3) Maintain 5-7cm water, 4) Fertilizer: 120kg N, 60kg P2O5, 40kg K2O per hectare, 5) Harvest when 80% grains turn golden (120-150 days)
For Basmati rice: Use varieties like Pusa 1121, Pusa 1509. Transplant in June-July with 20x15cm spacing. Apply less nitrogen (100kg/ha) for better aroma. Drain field 2 weeks before harvest!
Rice growing steps: Nursery preparation → Puddling (wet tillage) → Transplanting (2-3 seedlings per hill) → Water management (keep flooded) → Fertilizer in splits → Weed control → Harvest at maturity
Popular rice varieties: IR64 (115 days, high yield), Swarna (145 days, medium duration), Pusa Basmati 1121 (premium quality), MTU 7029 (Swarna Sub1 - flood tolerant). Choose based on your region!
Rice fertilizer schedule: 1/2 nitrogen at transplanting, 1/4 at tillering (21 days), 1/4 at panicle initiation (45 days). Apply full phosphorus and potassium at transplanting time!

Wheat cultivation: Sow in October-November. Seed rate 100kg/hectare. Row spacing 20-22cm. Fertilizer: 120kg N, 60kg P2O5, 40kg K2O per hectare. Need 4-6 irrigations. Harvest in March-April (120-140 days)
Wheat varieties: HD2967 (irrigated), PBW343 (rust resistant), DBW17 (heat tolerant), WH1105 (chapati quality). Choose certified seeds for better yield!

Wheat irrigation: 1st at Crown Root Initiation (20-25 days), 2nd at Tillering (40 days), 3rd at Jointing (60 days), 4th at Flowering (80 days), 5th at Milk stage (100 days), 6th at Dough stage (115 days)
Wheat fertilizer: Apply half nitrogen + full P&K at sowing. Remaining nitrogen at first irrigation (20-25 days). Use 120kg N, 60kg P2O5, 40kg K2O per hectare for good yield!
Wheat sowing: Timely sowing (Nov 1-15) gives best yield. Late sowing needs higher seed rate (125kg/ha). Use seed drill for uniform depth and spacing. Pre-sowing irrigation if soil is dry!

Tomato cultivation: Transplant 25-30 day seedlings. Spacing 60x45cm. Fertilizer: 150kg N, 75kg P2O5, 75kg K2O per hectare. Apply nitrogen in 3 splits. Need staking. Harvest when fruits turn red (70-90 days from transplanting)

Hybrid tomato varieties: Arka Rakshak (disease resistant, 70-75 tons/ha), Arka Samrat (nematode resistant), Pusa Hybrid 4 (heat tolerant), US 618 (determinate type). Use hybrid seeds for higher yield!

Tomato diseases: Early blight (spray Mancozeb 0.25%), Late blight (Cymoxanil+Mancozeb), Leaf curl virus (control whitefly with Imidacloprid), Bacterial wilt (use resistant variety). Spray preventively!
Tomato care: Mulching with black plastic increases yield. Drip irrigation saves water. Remove suckers from leaf axils. Stake plants for support. Spray calcium to prevent blossom end rot!
Season-wise tomato: Kharif (June-July sowing), Rabi (Oct-Nov sowing), Summer (Jan-Feb sowing). Rabi season gives best quality. Summer needs heat-tolerant varieties!

Potato cultivation: Plant in October-November. Use certified seed potatoes (2-2.5 tons/hectare). Spacing 60x20cm. Earthing up after 30 days. Fertilizer: 180kg N, 80kg P2O5, 100kg K2O per hectare. Harvest after 90-110 days
Potato varieties: Kufri Jyoti (early, 90 days), Kufri Pukhraj (chips making), Kufri Chandramukhi (processing), Kufri Badshah (late blight resistant). Choose based on use and season!
Potato fertilizer: Full P&K + 1/3 nitrogen at planting, 1/3 nitrogen at 30 days, 1/3 at 45 days. Use well-decomposed FYM 20-25 tons per hectare before planting!
Potato diseases: Late blight (most serious - spray Mancozeb or Metalaxyl+Mancozeb every 10 days in humid weather). Use resistant varieties like Kufri Giriraj. Remove infected plants immediately!
Seed potato treatment: Treat with Carbendazim 2g/kg before planting. Use 30-40g size tubers. Cut large tubers with 2-3 eyes, dry cut pieces 2-3 days before planting!

Onion cultivation: Transplant 40-45 day seedlings. Spacing 15x10cm. Fertilizer: 100kg N, 50kg P2O5, 50kg K2O per hectare in splits. Light irrigation every 7-10 days. Harvest when tops fall over (120-150 days)
Onion varieties: Pusa Red (Kharif, dark red), N-53 (Rabi, yellow, good storage), Bhima Super (white, export), Agrifound Dark Red (Rabi), Bhima Shakti (late Kharif, purple)
Onion seasons: Kharif (June-July sowing), Rabi (Nov-Dec), Late Kharif (Sept-Oct). Rabi season gives best storage quality!
Onion diseases: Purple blotch (spray Mancozeb), Stemphylium blight (Azoxystrobin), Thrips (Fipronil spray). Stop irrigation 15 days before harvest for better storage!
Onion storage: Cure bulbs in shade for 10-15 days. Store in ventilated room at 25-30°C. Properly cured N-53 variety can store 3-4 months!
Mango cultivation: Plant grafted saplings in July-August. Spacing 10x10m. Fertilizer per mature tree: 50kg FYM + 1.5kg N + 0.75kg P2O5 + 1.5kg K2O annually. Apply in 2 splits (June & October)
Mango varieties: Alphonso (Konkan, export quality), Dasheri (North India), Langra (Bihar, fiber-less), Kesar (Gujarat, saffron aroma), Chaunsa (Punjab), Amrapali (dwarf, high density)
Mango diseases: Powdery mildew (spray Sulfex 0.2%), Anthracnose (Copper oxychloride 0.3%), Mango hopper (Imidacloprid at flowering). Spray before monsoon!
Mango flowering: Flowers appear November-February. Apply Paclobutrazol in September for uniform flowering. Spray NAA 20ppm during flowering to reduce fruit drop!
Mango care: Prune trees for shape and light penetration. Mulch around trees. Irrigate during dry spells. Remove diseased branches. Protect from fruit flies using traps!

Banana cultivation: Plant tissue culture plants in Feb-March or June-July. Spacing 1.8x1.8m. Fertilizer per plant: 200g N, 60g P2O5, 300g K2O in 8-10 monthly splits. Regular irrigation (4-5 days). Harvest after 11-13 months
Banana varieties: Grand Naine (export quality, 12-13 months), Robusta (common, hardy, 12-15 months), Poovan (small sweet), Nendran (cooking, Kerala), Red banana (premium)
Tissue culture banana: Disease-free, uniform plants. Higher yield (40-50kg/plant vs 25-30kg conventional). Early bearing (11-12 months). Cost more but worth it!
Banana diseases: Panama wilt (use resistant variety), Sigatoka (spray Carbendazim), Bunchy top virus (remove infected plants + control aphids), Weevil (apply Carbofuran in soil)
Banana care: Desuckering (keep 1 follower), propping during fruiting, mulching with dry leaves, remove male bud after fruit formation, harvest when fingers are well-filled!
Chili cultivation: Transplant 30-35 day seedlings. Spacing 60x45cm. Fertilizer: 150kg N, 75kg P2O5, 75kg K2O per hectare. Apply nitrogen in 4-5 splits. Harvest green at 45 days, red at 80-90 days
Chili varieties: Byadgi (deep red color), Guntur Sannam (high pungency, export), Teja (super hot), Pusa Jwala (green chili), Wonder Hot (virus resistant), Kashmiri (mild, color)
Chili diseases: Leaf curl virus (control whitefly + remove infected plants), Anthracnose (Copper oxychloride), Powdery mildew (Sulfur spray), Die back (Bordeaux mixture)
Chili for green harvest: Pusa Jwala, G4, Arka Lohit varieties. Pick every 4-5 days when fruits reach full size. Yield 100-150 quintals per hectare!
Dry chili: Harvest when fruits turn red. Dry in sun for 7-10 days to 10% moisture. Properly dried chili prevents aflatoxin. Yield 15-20 quintals per hectare!
Cotton cultivation: Sow in May-June. Spacing 90x60cm for hybrids. Fertilizer: 120kg N, 60kg P2O5, 60kg K2O per hectare. Apply nitrogen in 3 splits. Need 5-6 irrigations. Duration 150-180 days
BT cotton: Genetically modified for bollworm resistance. Varieties: RCH-2, Ankur-651, MRC-7361. Higher yield 25-30 quintals/ha. Still need IPM for sucking pests!
Cotton pests: Pink bollworm (pheromone traps + spray), Whitefly (Thiamethoxam), Jassids (Imidacloprid), American bollworm (NPV + Bt). Follow 20% refuge strategy for BT cotton!
Cotton fertilizer: Apply nitrogen in 3 splits - basal, squaring stage, flowering stage. Use 10 tons FYM before planting. Critical irrigation at flowering and boll development!
Cotton harvesting: Pick when 50-60% bolls open. Multiple pickings (3-4 times) for better quality. Kapas yield 20-25 quintals/hectare in hybrids!

Sugarcane cultivation: Plant Feb-March or Sept-Oct. Use 3-bud setts (2-3 tons/hectare). Spacing 90cm rows. Fertilizer: 150kg N, 60kg P2O5, 60kg K2O per hectare. Earthing up at 90-120 days. Duration 10-12 months
Sugarcane varieties: CoJ 64 (mid-late, high sugar), Co 0238 (early, 10 months), Co 118 (waterlogging tolerant), CoLk 94184 (salt tolerant), Co 86032 (disease resistant)
Sugarcane fertilizer: Apply nitrogen in 3 splits - at planting, 60 days, 120 days. Need 10-12 irrigations throughout growing period!
Sugarcane diseases: Red rot (most serious - use resistant variety + Carbendazim), Smut (remove whips + spray Propiconazole), Wilt (soil treatment). Use disease-free setts!
Ratoon management: After harvest, gap filling within 15 days. Apply higher nitrogen (180kg/ha). First ratoon gives 80-90% plant crop yield. Take 3-4 ratoons!

Mustard cultivation: Rabi crop (Oct-Nov sowing). Varieties: Pusa Bold (95-100 days), Varuna (125-130 days), RH 30 (brown, 130 days). Seed rate: 4-5 kg/hectare. Spacing: 30-45cm rows. Harvest when pods turn yellowish-brown!
Mustard fertilizer: 100-120kg N, 40kg P2O5, 20kg K2O per hectare. Apply half nitrogen at sowing, half at 30-35 days. Needs 2-3 irrigations (pre-flowering & pod filling). Thinning at 20-25 days!

Mustard varieties: Pusa Bold (yellow, early, 18-20q/ha), Varuna (brown, late, high oil), Pusa Mustard 25 (aphid tolerant), RH 30 (brown sarson), Kranti (white rust resistant), Pusa Agrani (early 90 days)!
Mustard diseases: White rust (spray Metalaxyl), Alternaria blight (Mancozeb), Powdery mildew (Sulfur). Aphids major pest - spray Dimethoate or use resistant varieties. Spray at flowering initiation!
Mustard harvesting: Harvest when 75% pods turn yellowish-brown, seeds rattle inside pods. Cut plants early morning. Dry 3-4 days, thresh carefully. Yield: 15-20 quintals/hectare. Oil content: 37-42%!

Groundnut cultivation: Kharif crop (June-July sowing). Seed rate: 100-120kg/hectare (kernels) or 140-160kg (pods). Spacing: 30x10cm. Well-drained sandy loam soil. Harvest at 100-130 days when leaves turn yellow!
Groundnut varieties: TG37A (Spanish type, 105 days), TAG24 (high oil), GG20 (drought tolerant), K6 (bold kernel), ICGV91114 (high yield). Use certified seeds only!
Groundnut fertilizer: Low nitrogen (20kg N), higher phosphorus (60kg P2O5), 40kg K2O per hectare. Apply gypsum 500kg/ha at flowering for pod filling!
Groundnut diseases: Tikka disease (spray Carbendazim), Collar rot (seed treatment), Rust (Mancozeb spray). Seed treatment with Thiram 3g/kg + Rhizobium culture!
Groundnut care: Earthing up at 30 days, spray calcium (gypsum) at flowering, maintain soil moisture during peg penetration, harvest when 75% pods mature!
Soybean cultivation: Kharif crop (June-July sowing). Seed rate: 60-80kg/hectare. Spacing: 45x5cm. Duration: 90-120 days. Needs well-drained soil. Harvest when leaves turn yellow and pods dry!
Soybean varieties: JS335 (90-95 days, popular), JS9560 (high yield), NRC37 (disease resistant), Bragg (old reliable), Pusa9712 (yellow mosaic resistant)!
Soybean fertilizer: 20kg N (or Rhizobium inoculation), 60-80kg P2O5, 40kg K2O per hectare. Soybean fixes nitrogen, so low nitrogen needed!
Soybean diseases: Yellow mosaic virus (resistant varieties + whitefly control), Stem rot (Carbendazim), Rust (Hexaconazole). Seed treatment essential!
Soybean care: Weed control first 30 days critical, avoid waterlogging, spray micronutrients (Zinc, Iron) if deficient. Yield: 20-30 quintals/hectare!
Maize cultivation: Kharif (June-July) and Rabi (Oct-Nov). Seed rate: 20-25kg/hectare for hybrids. Spacing: 60x20cm. Duration: 90-120 days. Needs good drainage and fertility!
Maize varieties: Vivek Hybrid 9 (early), DHM117 (high yield), HQPM1 (quality protein), NK6240 (private hybrid), P3522 (pop corn). Choose based on purpose and season!
Maize fertilizer: 150kg N, 75kg P2O5, 75kg K2O per hectare. Apply nitrogen in 3 splits - basal (1/3), knee-high (1/3), tasseling (1/3). Zinc application important!
Maize diseases: Turcicum leaf blight (Mancozeb), Maydis leaf blight (resistant varieties), Stem borer (Carbofuran). Seed treatment with Thiram!
Maize care: Thinning at 10-15 days, earthing up at 30 days, detasseling for seed production, timely irrigation at tasseling & grain filling. Yield: 60-80 quintals/hectare!
Urea (46% Nitrogen): Most common nitrogen fertilizer. Apply in splits during crop growth. Rice: 130kg/acre, Wheat: 110kg/acre, Vegetables: 40-50kg/acre. Never apply all at once or near seeds!

Urea timing for wheat: 1/3 at sowing, 1/3 at first irrigation (21 days), 1/3 at second irrigation (40 days). For rice: 1/2 at transplanting, 1/4 at tillering (21 days), 1/4 at panicle initiation (50 days)
Neem coated urea: Urea coated with neem oil for slow release. Benefits: Better nitrogen efficiency (85% vs 65%), less quantity needed (10-15% less), reduced losses. Government promoted!
Urea for vegetables: Tomato (50kg/acre in 3 splits), Potato (60kg/acre in 3 splits), Onion (40kg/acre in 2 splits), Cabbage (50kg/acre in 3 splits). Apply 6 inches away from plant!
Urea precautions: Apply on moist soil + irrigate immediately. Avoid over-application (promotes pests). Don't mix with SSP. Apply in evening/morning. Split application is better!
DAP (18% N, 46% P2O5): Main phosphorus fertilizer. Apply only at sowing/planting time as basal dose. Wheat: 60kg/acre, Rice: 50kg/acre, Potato: 80kg/acre. Mix well in soil!
DAP application: Apply ONLY at sowing time! Phosphorus doesn't move in soil, later application is useless. For row crops: place 2-3 inches below and beside seed!
DAP for crops: Wheat (60kg/acre), Paddy (50kg/acre), Maize (50kg/acre), Cotton (40kg/acre), Vegetables (60-70kg/acre), Pulses (40kg/acre). Always at planting time!
DAP vs Urea: DAP has N (18%) + P (46%), apply at sowing. Urea only N (46%), apply in splits. Both needed! DAP for roots/flowers, Urea for leaves/growth!
DAP precautions: Never top dress (waste of money). Don't touch seeds (burns). Mix well in soil. In alkaline soils, use with organic matter for better phosphorus availability!
MOP (Muriate of Potash - 60% K2O): Main potassium fertilizer. Improves fruit quality, disease resistance, drought tolerance. Paddy: 35kg/acre, Wheat: 25kg/acre, Potato: 50kg/acre
MOP application: Apply in 2 splits - half at sowing/planting, half at flowering/fruiting. For fruit trees: apply in monsoon (June-July). Broadcast and mix in soil!
Potash benefits: Improves fruit size, color & sweetness. Increases sugar in sugarcane. Strengthens stems (prevents lodging). Critical for potato, banana, mango, citrus!
MOP for fruits: Mango (1-2kg/tree in June-July), Banana (200g/plant monthly), Citrus (1kg/tree/year in 3 splits), Pomegranate (500g/plant). Apply 1 foot away from trunk!
Potash deficiency signs: Brown leaf edges, weak stems, small fruits, poor color. Use MOP to correct. Don't apply near seed or in saline soils!
NPK Complex: Contains all three nutrients (N-P-K). Common grades: 10-26-26, 20-20-0, 12-32-16, 19-19-19. Easier application, balanced nutrition. Apply as basal dose!
NPK numbers: First = Nitrogen (leaf growth), Second = Phosphorus (roots, flowers), Third = Potassium (fruits, disease resistance). Example: 19-19-19 = equal, good for all crops!
NPK for vegetables: Leafy crops: high N (20-10-10), Fruiting crops: balanced (19-19-19) or high K (10-10-20), Root crops: high P (10-20-10)
Common NPK grades: 10-26-26 (general purpose), 20-20-0 (wheat, cereals), 12-32-16 (high phosphorus), 19-19-19 (all-purpose vegetables), 14-35-14 (flowering crops)
NPK application: Broadcast and mix before planting for field crops. Band placement 2-3 inches beside seed for row crops. For vegetables: apply at bed preparation!
Organic fertilizers: FYM (10-15 tons/hectare), Vermicompost (2-3 tons/hectare), Neem cake (200kg/hectare). Slow release, improves soil health, microbial activity!
FYM (Farm Yard Manure): Well-decomposed cow dung + urine + bedding. NPK 0.5-0.2-0.5%. Apply 15-20 tons/hectare 2-3 weeks before planting. Improves soil structure!
Vermicompost: Premium organic (earthworm castings). NPK 1.5-1-1. Use 2-3 tons/hectare. Contains growth hormones, enzymes, beneficial bacteria. Perfect for organic vegetables!
Jeevamrut: 10kg cow dung + 10L cow urine + 2kg jaggery + 2kg pulse flour + 1kg soil in 200L water. Ferment 7 days. Apply 200L/acre with irrigation!
Green manure: Dhaincha (50kg/hectare), Sunhemp (25kg/hectare), Cowpea (30kg/hectare). Sow before monsoon, incorporate at flowering (45 days). Adds nitrogen and organic matter!
Micronutrients: Zinc, Iron, Manganese, Copper, Boron, Molybdenum. Small quantity but essential! Zinc most deficient in rice & wheat. Apply via soil or foliar spray!
Zinc deficiency: Rice (khaira disease) - stunted growth, brown spots. Wheat - white/yellow leaves. Soil: ZnSO4 25kg/hectare. Foliar: 0.5% ZnSO4 + 0.25% lime!
Iron deficiency: Young leaves turn yellow (chlorosis), veins stay green. Common in alkaline soils. Foliar spray Ferrous sulfate 0.5% or Chelated iron 0.2%. Repeat 2-3 times!
Boron deficiency: Hollow stem in cauliflower, heart rot in beet, fruit drop in tomato. Soil: Borax 10kg/hectare (once in 3 years). Foliar: 0.2% borax!
Micronutrient spray: Multi-micronutrient mixture (Zn, Fe, Mn, B, Mo) - 2.5kg in 500L water per hectare. Spray at tillering, flowering, grain filling. Add wetting agent!
Rice Blast: Most serious fungal disease! Leaf blast = spindle-shaped spots, gray center. Neck blast = graying of neck, grains don't fill. Spray Tricyclazole 0.6g/L at tillering, booting, heading!
Blast control: Preventive spray - Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6g/L at tillering, booting, heading stages. Curative - Kasugamycin + Copper oxychloride. Spray 3 times at 10-day intervals!
Blast management: Use resistant varieties (Pusa 1121, Pusa 1509), balanced fertilization (avoid excess nitrogen), don't let water stagnate, remove infected plants immediately!
Neck blast: Most damaging! Appears during flowering. Entire panicle becomes white. Spray Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole at 50% flowering. Repeat after 10 days!
Blast prevention: Seed treatment with Carbendazim (2g/kg), avoid late nitrogen, silicon application improves resistance, maintain 2-3cm water depth!
Bacterial Blight (BLB): Yellow to white lesions on leaf margins/tips, wavy pattern. Kresek phase = rapid wilting. Use resistant varieties (Pusa 1509, Pusa 1121)!
BLB control: Seed treatment with Streptocycline (25ppm for 24hrs). Spray Copper oxychloride 0.3% + Streptocycline 100ppm at tillering and booting!
BLB management: Don't apply excess nitrogen. Drain water for 3-4 days after transplanting. Spray Plantomycin 100ppm at tillering & booting!
BLB prevention: Use disease-free seeds, avoid deep water (5-7cm enough), balanced fertilization, crop rotation, remove infected stubbles after harvest!
Chemical control BLB: Streptocycline + Tetracycline (3g in 10L water) or Copper hydroxide (3g/L). Spray 2-3 times at 10-day intervals from tillering!
Stem Borer: Most destructive rice pest! Dead heart (young stage - central shoot dries), White head (panicle turns white). Spray Cartap hydrochloride or Chlorantraniliprole!
Stem borer control: Cartap hydrochloride 4G (10kg/hectare at tillering) or Chlorantraniliprole 0.4G (4kg/acre). Can also spray Chlorpyriphos 2ml/L at tillering!
Stem borer management: Light traps for moths, remove grasses, pheromone traps (8/acre), release Trichogramma parasitoids (50,000/acre)!
Stem borer spray: Cartap 50SP (1g/L) or Fipronil 5SC (2ml/L) or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5SC (0.3ml/L). Spray at early vegetative stage within 30 days!
Prevention: Early transplanting, clip seedling tips (removes eggs), avoid ratoon cropping, summer plowing, use resistant varieties (Swarna Sub1)!
Brown Plant Hopper (BPH): Sucks sap from stem base. Hopper burn = patches turn brown. Spray Imidacloprid 0.5ml/L or Buprofezin 1.5ml/L at lower portion of plant!
BPH control: Imidacloprid 17.8SL (0.5ml/L) or Buprofezin 25SC (1.5ml/L) or Pymetrozine 50WG (0.6g/L). Spray at base and water surface. Avoid prophylactic spraying!
BPH management: Don't use excess nitrogen, maintain thin water layer, conserve natural enemies (spiders), use resistant varieties (Swarna Sub1)!
Economic Threshold: Spray only when 10-15 hoppers per hill at vegetative stage, 5-10 per hill at reproductive stage. Don't spray routinely!
BPH resistant varieties: Vikramarya, DRR Dhan 45, CR Dhan 800. Use in endemic areas. Thiamethoxam as seedling root dip helps!
Yellow Rust: Most serious wheat disease! Yellow-orange pustules in stripes. Spreads in cool humid weather (10-15°C). Can reduce yield 40-50%!
Yellow rust control: Propiconazole 1ml/L or Tebuconazole 1g/L or Trifloxystrobin+Tebuconazole 0.5ml/L. Spray when 5-10% plants infected. Repeat after 15 days if needed!
Rust management: Use resistant varieties (PBW 725, HD 3086, DBW 187), timely sowing (Nov 1-15), balanced fertilization, avoid excess nitrogen!
Preventive spray: If rust history, spray Sulfex (Sulfur) 2g/L at tillering. For confirmed infection, use Propiconazole or Tebuconazole. Spray morning/evening!
Resistant varieties: HD 3086 (rust + heat tolerant), PBW 725 (stripe rust resistant), DBW 187, WH 1124 (dual rust resistant). Use certified seeds!
Powdery Mildew: White powdery coating on leaves. Common on cucurbits, peas, mango. Spray Sulfur 80WP (2g/L) or Hexaconazole (2ml/L) at first appearance!
Mildew control: Sulfur 2g/L or Azoxystrobin 1ml/L. Spray both leaf surfaces. Repeat every 7-10 days. May need 3-4 sprays!
Cultural control: Proper spacing, avoid overhead irrigation, remove infected parts, don't over-fertilize nitrogen, grow in sunny locations!
Home remedy: Milk spray (1:10 milk:water) or Baking soda (1 tablespoon + 1 teaspoon oil per liter). Works for mild infections in home gardens!
Prevention: Plant resistant varieties, avoid crowding, prune for air circulation, water at base, apply Sulfur preventively in disease-prone areas!
Aphids (Chepti): Small insects (green/black/brown). Suck sap, secrete honeydew, transmit viruses. Spray Imidacloprid 0.5ml/L or Thiamethoxam 0.5g/L on leaf underside!
Aphid control: Imidacloprid 17.8SL (0.5ml/L) or Dimethoate 30EC (2ml/L). Spray thoroughly on leaf underside. One spray usually sufficient. Avoid during flowering!
Natural control: Spray water forcefully, neem oil 3ml/L, soap solution 5g/L. Encourage ladybirds, lacewings - they eat aphids!
Mustard aphid: Peak in Jan-Feb. Spray Dimethoate 2ml/L or Imidacloprid 0.5ml/L when 10% plants infested. One spray at flowering initiation!
Prevention: Yellow sticky traps, reflective mulch, companion planting (garlic, onion), avoid excess nitrogen, conserve ladybirds!
Whitefly: Tiny white flying insects. Major problem: transmit viruses (Leaf curl in chili/tomato, Yellow mosaic in okra). Spray Spiromesifen or Pyriproxyfen!
Whitefly control: Spiromesifen 22.9SC (1ml/L) or Pyriproxyfen 10EC (1ml/L) or Diafenthiuron 50WP (1g/L). Spray leaf undersides thoroughly!
Cotton whitefly: Spray Imidacloprid 0.5ml/L or Thiamethoxam 0.5g/L at first appearance. If virus symptoms, spray Acetamiprid 0.5g/L. Remove infected plants!
Whitefly management: Yellow sticky traps, reflective silver mulch, remove weeds, avoid late planting, use virus-resistant varieties!
Neem control: Neem oil 3ml/L + Azadirachtin 2ml/L. Spray weekly as preventive. For severe infestation, use chemical insecticides!
Fruit Borer (Helicoverpa): Caterpillar bores into fruits/pods. Damages tomato, okra, chili. Spray Emamectin benzoate 0.5g/L or Spinosad 0.3ml/L at flowering!
Fruit borer control: Emamectin benzoate 5SG (0.5g/L) or Indoxacarb 14.5SC (1ml/L). Spray at flower initiation, repeat every 10-15 days. Need 3-4 sprays!
Integrated management: Pheromone traps (4-5/acre), NPV spray (250LE/ha with jaggery), neem extract (5%), bird perches, marigold as trap crop!
Tomato borer: Handpick damaged fruits. Spray Chlorantraniliprole 0.3ml/L or Flubendiamide 0.25g/L at flowering. Rotate insecticides!
Organic control: Bt spray (2g/L), NSKE (5%), NPV (250LE/ha). Spray in evening. Release Trichogramma parasitoids (50,000/acre)!
Termites (Deemak): Underground insects. Damage roots, seeds, stems. Major problem in sugarcane, wheat. Apply Chlorpyriphos 2.5L/ha as soil drench before sowing!
Termite control: Chlorpyriphos 20EC (2.5L in 400L water per hectare, soil drench) or Fipronil 5SC (2L/ha). Apply before sowing or with first irrigation!
Sugarcane termite: Treat setts with Chlorpyriphos (2.5ml/L) before planting. Soak 10 minutes. Or apply with irrigation at planting!
Termite prevention: Deep summer plowing (exposes colonies), remove crop residue, avoid fresh organic matter at sowing, use well-decomposed FYM!
Organic control: Wood ash in soil, neem cake (200kg/ha), castor cake. Destroy termite mounds near fields. Flood fields where possible!
Root-knot Nematodes: Microscopic worms. Attack roots, form galls/knots. Major in tomato, okra, banana. Apply Carbofuran 3G (1kg/acre) or neem cake (200kg/acre)!
Nematode control: Carbofuran 3G (1kg/acre at planting) or Phorate 10G (10kg/acre). Bio-control: Paecilomyces lilacinus (5kg/acre with FYM)!
Cultural management: Crop rotation (maize, sorghum), summer plowing, flooding, grow marigold (traps & kills nematodes)!
Banana nematode: Use tissue culture plants. Apply Carbofuran 3G (50g/plant) every 3 months. Mulch with neem/marigold leaves!
Resistant varieties: Tomato - Pusa Sheetal, Okra - Arka Anamika, Brinjal - IIHR-6. Use neem cake 200kg/ha. Green manuring with mustard reduces nematodes!
Drip Irrigation: Water directly to roots through drippers. Water saving 40-70%! Increases yield 20-50%. Best for vegetables, fruits, sugarcane, cotton!
Drip components: Water source → Pump → Filter → Fertilizer tank → Main line → Sub-main → Lateral → Drippers (4LPH common). Need pressure regulator for hills!
Drip spacing: Vegetables: Lateral 1.5-2ft, dripper 30-40cm. Widely spaced (tomato): Lateral 5-6ft, dripper 50-60cm. Closely spaced (onion): drippers 20-30cm!
Drip cost: Rs.45,000-60,000 per acre (all components). Subsidy 55-90% available! Check with agriculture department for schemes!
Drip maintenance: Clean filters weekly, check for clogs, flush system monthly, acid treatment yearly, replace laterals every 4-5 years!
Sprinkler Irrigation: Mimics rainfall. Suitable for all crops, all soil types. Water saving 30-40%. Types: Mini (vegetables), Medium (cereals), Rain gun (large fields)!
Sprinkler types: Mini (4-6m radius, vegetables), Medium (8-12m, field crops), Rain gun (30-50m, sugarcane). Choose based on crop and field size!
Sprinkler cost: Mini - Rs.30,000-40,000/acre, Medium - Rs.25,000-35,000/acre, Rain gun - Rs.40,000-50,000/acre. Government subsidy 50-80% available!
Sprinkler for wheat: Spacing 12x12m or 15x15m. Medium pressure (2-3 kg/cm²). Apply 50mm water per irrigation. Saves 30-35% water, increases yield!
Sprinkler vs Drip: Drip - row crops, vegetables, fruits, water saving 50-70%. Sprinkler - all crops, cereals, pulses, water saving 30-40%, suitable for wheat/mustard!
Soil Testing: Essential! Tests pH, organic carbon, NPK, micronutrients. Collect samples before planting. Test every 2-3 years. FREE at government labs!
Sample collection: Collect from 8-10 spots, 6-8 inch depth, mix well, take 500g sample. Avoid manure heaps, boundaries. Air dry, pack in cloth bag!
Testing labs: Government agriculture offices (KVK, District Agriculture Office), Universities. FREE at government labs! Private Rs.100-500. Results in 7-15 days!
Soil Health Card: FREE soil testing every 2 years! Apply at soilhealth.dac.gov.in or agriculture office. Card shows nutrients + fertilizer recommendations!
Interpreting results: Low N (add urea), Low P (add DAP), Low K (add MOP), pH<5.5 (add lime 500kg/acre), pH>8 (add gypsum 500kg/acre)!
Vermicompost: Premium organic fertilizer by earthworms (Eisenia fetida). NPK 1.5-2-1.5 + growth hormones. Use 2-3 tons/hectare!
Making vermicompost: Cement tank 10x3x2ft. Layer: 6-inch cow dung → 3-inch farm waste → release 2000 worms → cover with gunny → spray water daily → ready in 60-70 days!
Vermicompost worms: Eisenia fetida (red/tiger worms). Buy from KVK (Rs.400-600/kg, ~1500 worms). Feed on cow dung, kitchen waste, farm residue!
Vermicompost business: Cost Rs.4-6/kg, selling Rs.12-18/kg. From 10x3ft bed: 150-200kg per 70 days. Set up 10-20 beds for commercial production!
Using vermicompost: Mix 10-20% in potting soil. Field: 2-3 tons/hectare. Vegetables: 1-2 tons/acre. Tea: 1kg in 10L water, filter, spray!
Greenhouse/Polyhouse: Controlled environment. Protects from weather, pests. Grow high-value crops year-round! Types: Naturally ventilated (cheaper), Fan-pad cooled (controlled)!
Polyhouse cost: Naturally ventilated Rs.700-900/m² (Rs.28-35 lakh/acre), Fan-pad Rs.1400-1800/m² (Rs.56-72 lakh/acre). Government subsidy 50-90% available!
Greenhouse crops: Tomato (150-200 tons/ha vs 50-60 open), Capsicum (export quality), Cucumber, Rose, Gerbera, Seedling nursery. Need training!
Greenhouse management: Temperature control (vents, fans), Humidity 60-70%, Drip + fertigation, Soilless cultivation (cocopeat), IPM (sticky traps). Regular monitoring!
Greenhouse tomato: Indeterminate hybrids. Spacing 45x45cm, single stem, 12-14 months crop. Yield 15-20kg/plant. Need training, pollination!
PMFBY (Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana): Government crop insurance. Premium: Kharif 2%, Rabi 1.5%, Horticulture 5%. Covers natural calamities, pests, diseases!
How to enroll: Visit bank, cooperative, or CSC center. Documents: Aadhaar, land records, bank account, sowing certificate. Deadline before sowing season!
Coverage: Prevented sowing, standing crop loss, post-harvest loss (14 days), localized calamity. Sum insured based on scale of finance!
Claim process: Inform within 72 hours of loss. Call toll-free 14447 or use Crop Insurance App. Document damage with photos. Assessment by insurance company!
Premium example: For Rs.1 lakh sum insured - Kharif Rs.2000, Rabi Rs.1500, Horticulture Rs.5000. Government pays remaining premium!
PM-KISAN: Rs.6000/year direct transfer in 3 installments. Register at pmkisan.gov.in with Aadhaar, land records!
Kisan Credit Card (KCC): Crop loan at 4% interest (with subsidy). Apply at any bank. Limit based on land holding and crop!
Subsidies available: Seeds (50-75%), Drip irrigation (55-90%), Farm machinery (50-80%), Solar pump (60-90%), Polyhouse (50-90%). Check state schemes!
Soil Health Card: Free soil testing + fertilizer recommendation. Apply at soilhealth.dac.gov.in!
e-NAM: Sell produce online at better prices. Register at enam.gov.in. 1000+ mandis connected!
Seed Treatment: Treating seeds with fungicide/insecticide/bio-agent before sowing. Protects from diseases, improves germination!
Fungicide treatment: Rice - Carbendazim 2g/kg. Wheat - Vitavax Power 2.5g/kg. Cotton - Imidacloprid + Carbendazim. Soak 24hrs or dust dry!
Biological treatment: Trichoderma viride (4g/kg seed), Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/kg), Azospirillum + PSB (25g/kg for pulses). Organic alternative!
Seed priming: Soak seeds 8-12 hours, shade dry. Benefits: Faster germination, uniform emergence, better vigor. Good for old seeds!
Treatment method: Dry dressing - mix in polybag. Wet treatment - dissolve in water, coat, shade dry. Use recommended dose only!
Weed control methods: Manual weeding, mechanical cultivation, chemical herbicides, mulching. Integrated approach best!
Rice herbicides: Pre-emergence - Pretilachlor (1L/ha within 3 days). Post-emergence - Bispyribac sodium (25g/ha at 15-25 DAT). Apply in standing water!
Wheat herbicides: Pre-emergence - Pendimethalin (1L/ha within 3 days). Post-emergence - 2,4-D (0.5kg/ha at 30-35 days) or Sulfosulfuron (25g/ha)!
Vegetable weed control: Manual weeding + mulching best. Pre-emergence Pendimethalin for transplanted crops. Avoid herbicide on leafy vegetables!
Weed prevention: Use certified weed-free seeds, proper field preparation, timely sowing, crop rotation, maintain good crop stand!

patterns: How to know crop is ready
responses: Rice harvest: When 80% grains turn golden yellow, moisture 20-22%. Cut, dry to 14% moisture for storage. Avoid delay (shattering loss)!
Wheat harvest: When grains hard, moisture 12-14%, straw golden yellow. Combine or manual cutting. Dry properly before storage!
Tomato harvest: For local market - red ripe. For distant market - breaker stage (pink). Handle carefully, grade by size and color!
Potato harvest: When leaves yellow and dry. Cure in shade 10-15 days. Store at 2-4°C for table, 10-12°C for seed. Remove damaged ones!
General tips: Harvest in morning, use sharp tools, avoid damage, dry properly, grade before storage, maintain cleanliness!
Grain storage basics: Clean and dry grain (moisture 12-14% for cereals, 8-9% for oilseeds). Clean storage structure. Stack on platforms!
Storage pests: Rice weevil, Khapra beetle, Lesser grain borer. Control: Fumigation with Aluminum phosphide (3g/ton), or mix neem leaves!
Traditional storage: Mix dried neem leaves (1kg per quintal), or use neem oil coating. Works for home storage!
Hermetic storage: Airtight bags/containers. No oxygen = no pests. Good for seed storage and organic produce!
Warehouse tips: Stack on dunnage (raised platform), maintain gap from walls, regular inspection, FIFO system, prevent moisture and rodents!
Essential nutrients: Macro (N, P, K, Ca, Mg, S) - needed in large amounts. Micro (Fe, Zn, Mn, Cu, B, Mo, Cl) - small amounts but critical!
Nitrogen (N): For leaf growth, green color. Deficiency: pale yellow leaves, stunted growth. Source: Urea, DAP, organic manures!
Phosphorus (P): For root development, flowering, fruiting. Deficiency: purple leaves, poor flowering. Source: DAP, SSP, bone meal!
Potassium (K): For fruit quality, disease resistance, drought tolerance. Deficiency: brown leaf edges, weak stems. Source: MOP, SOP!
Deficiency diagnosis: N - older leaves yellow first. P - purple tint, poor roots. K - leaf edges brown. Fe/Zn - young leaves yellow, veins green!
Organic farming: No synthetic chemicals. Use organic manures (FYM, vermicompost), bio-pesticides, crop rotation, green manuring!
Starting organic: Conversion period 2-3 years. Start with soil building - FYM, vermicompost, green manuring. Gradually reduce chemicals!
Organic manures: FYM (10-15 tons/ha), Vermicompost (2-3 tons/ha), Green manure (dhaincha, sunhemp), Neem cake (200kg/ha)!
Organic pest control: Neem oil, Panchgavya, Bt spray, Trichoderma, beneficial insects. Trap crops, pheromone traps!
Organic certification: Apply to agencies like Ecocert, OneCert, Control Union. Maintain records, follow standards. Premium price 20-30% higher!
Essential machinery: Tractor (20-50 HP based on land), Cultivator, Rotavator, Seed drill, Sprayer (manual/power), Thresher/Combine!
Tractor selection: Small farms (2-5 acres) - 20-30 HP. Medium (5-15 acres) - 35-45 HP. Large (15+ acres) - 50+ HP. Consider soil type and implements!
Machinery subsidy: 50-80% subsidy on sprayers, rotavators, seed drills, power tillers. Apply through agriculture department or SMAM portal!
Custom hiring: Rent machinery from CHC (Custom Hiring Centre). Cheaper than owning. Available at subsidized rates in most districts!
Maintenance tips: Regular servicing, clean after use, proper storage, check oil/fuel, sharpen blades, replace worn parts timely!
Monsoon farming: Kharif crops (June-October) - rice, maize, cotton, soybean. Ensure drainage, watch for diseases in humid conditions!
Rabi season: October-March crops - wheat, mustard, chickpea, peas. Need irrigation. Cold nights good for flowering!
Drought management: Mulching, drip irrigation, drought-tolerant varieties, reduce plant population, foliar spray of potassium!
Frost protection: Cover crops with straw/cloth at night, light irrigation in evening (releases heat), avoid low-lying areas, smoke/fires upwind!
Heat stress: Mulching, frequent light irrigation, shade nets for vegetables, avoid mid-day operations, harvest early morning!
Companion planting: Growing complementary crops together. Benefits: pest control, better yield, soil improvement, space utilization!
Good combinations: Tomato + Basil (repels pests), Corn + Beans + Squash (Three Sisters), Onion + Carrot (confuse pests), Marigold with any (pest deterrent)!
Common intercrops: Sugarcane + Potato/Onion, Cotton + Groundnut, Maize + Pulses, Banana + Ginger, Mango + Legumes (young orchard)!
Benefits: Legumes fix nitrogen for cereals, tall crops shade short ones, deep-rooted crops bring up nutrients, diversity confuses pests!
Avoid together: Tomato + Cabbage (attract same pests), Onion + Beans (growth inhibition), Potato + Tomato (same diseases)!

Papaya cultivation: Plant seedlings in Feb-March or Sept-Oct. Spacing 2x2m. Duration: First harvest 9-10 months. Continuous harvest for 2-3 years. Well-drained soil essential!
Papaya varieties: Red Lady (hybrid, sweet, 12-15kg fruits), Taiwan 786 (popular, disease tolerant), Pusa Dwarf (short, early bearing), Coorg Honey Dew (local, sweet)!
Papaya fertilizer: 200g N, 250g P2O5, 250g K2O per plant per year in 4-5 splits. Apply FYM 10kg/plant at planting. Avoid waterlogging!
Papaya diseases: Ring spot virus (most serious - resistant varieties + aphid control), Foot rot (avoid waterlogging + Copper fungicide), Powdery mildew (Sulfur spray)!
Papaya care: Male plant ratio 1:10, remove extra males. Support with stakes. Harvest when yellow patches appear. Handle carefully - soft skin!
Guava cultivation: Plant in monsoon (July-Aug) or Feb-March. Spacing 6x6m for regular, 3x3m for high density. First fruiting 3-4 years (grafted), earlier than seed!
Guava varieties: Allahabad Safeda (white flesh, sweet), L-49 (Lucknow-49, pink flesh), Arka Mridula (seedless), Pant Prabhat (pink, high yield), VNR Bihi (pink, commercial)!
Guava fertilizer: Per tree per year - 10-15kg FYM, 300g N, 150g P2O5, 300g K2O. Apply in 3 splits (March, June, September). Increase with age!
Guava diseases: Wilt (use resistant rootstock + Trichoderma), Fruit fly (methyl eugenol traps + bagging), Anthracnose (Carbendazim spray)!
Guava care: Pruning for shape, remove water shoots. Bahar treatment for off-season crop. Fruit bagging for quality. Pick when light green to yellow!
Cabbage cultivation: Cool season crop. Transplant 30-35 day seedlings in Oct-Nov (Rabi). Spacing 45x45cm. Duration 90-120 days. Needs rich, well-drained soil!
Cabbage varieties: Golden Acre (early, 70 days), Pride of India (mid-season), Pusa Mukta (heat tolerant), Quisto F1 (hybrid, uniform), Green Express (early hybrid)!
Cabbage fertilizer: 100kg N, 50kg P2O5, 50kg K2O per hectare. Apply nitrogen in 3 splits - transplanting, 30 days, 60 days. FYM 20-25 tons/ha!
Cabbage diseases: Black rot (hot water seed treatment + copper spray), Club root (lime application + crop rotation), Downy mildew (Mancozeb spray)!
Cabbage pests: Diamond back moth (DBM) - most serious. Spray Spinosad or Emamectin. Aphids - Imidacloprid. Monitor regularly, rotate insecticides!
Cauliflower cultivation: Cool season crop. Early (Sept-Oct transplanting), Mid (Oct-Nov), Late (Nov-Dec). Spacing 45x45cm. Duration 90-120 days based on variety!
Cauliflower varieties: Pusa Snowball-1 (late, large curd), Pusa Kartik (early), Pusa Sharad (mid-season), Snowking F1 (hybrid), Amazing F1 (heat tolerant hybrid)!
Cauliflower fertilizer: 120kg N, 60kg P2O5, 60kg K2O per hectare. Nitrogen in 3 splits. Apply Boron (2kg Borax/ha) to prevent hollow stem!
Cauliflower diseases: Black rot (seed treatment + copper), Soft rot (avoid injury), Downy mildew (Metalaxyl spray). Blanching - tie leaves over curd for white color!
Cauliflower care: Protect curd from sun (tie leaves), regular irrigation, avoid waterlogging. Harvest when curd is compact before loose. Handle carefully!
Brinjal cultivation: Transplant 30-35 day seedlings. Kharif (June-July), Rabi (Oct-Nov), Summer (Jan-Feb). Spacing 60x45cm. Long duration crop (6-8 months harvest)!
Brinjal varieties: Pusa Purple Long (long purple), Pusa Purple Cluster (small, cluster), Pusa Uttam (round), Arka Shirish (bacterial wilt resistant), Punjab Sadabahar (round, purple)!
Brinjal fertilizer: 150kg N, 100kg P2O5, 50kg K2O per hectare. Apply nitrogen in 3-4 splits. FYM 25-30 tons/ha at planting!
Brinjal diseases: Bacterial wilt (use resistant variety + crop rotation), Phomopsis blight (Carbendazim spray), Little leaf (control jassids). Fruit borer major pest - Bt spray!
Brinjal care: Staking for hybrid varieties, regular picking encourages more fruiting, remove damaged fruits, maintain good drainage. Pick when glossy, before dull!
Okra cultivation: Warm season crop. Sow directly in Feb-March (summer) and June-July (Kharif). Spacing 45x30cm. Duration 90-120 days. Pick every 2-3 days!
Okra varieties: Pusa Sawani (popular, ridged), Arka Anamika (YVMV resistant), Parbhani Kranti (high yield), VRO-6 (YVMV tolerant), Namdhari NS-811 (hybrid)!
Okra fertilizer: 100kg N, 50kg P2O5, 50kg K2O per hectare. Half nitrogen at sowing, half at flowering. Seed rate 8-10kg/hectare!
Okra diseases: Yellow vein mosaic virus (YVMV - most serious, resistant varieties + whitefly control), Root rot (avoid waterlogging), Powdery mildew (Sulfur spray)!
Okra care: Pick tender fruits daily (become fibrous if left), remove virus-infected plants, control whitefly for YVMV. Soak seeds 24 hours before sowing for better germination!
Pea cultivation: Cool season crop. Sow Oct-Nov (Rabi). Spacing 30x10cm. Duration 90-130 days based on variety. Needs support for tall varieties!
Pea varieties: Arkel (early, dwarf, 60 days), Azad P-1 (mid-season), Pusa Pragati (70 days), Bonneville (late, tall), Palam Priya (garden pea)!
Pea fertilizer: 25kg N, 60kg P2O5, 40kg K2O per hectare. Pea fixes nitrogen - less N needed. Seed inoculation with Rhizobium helps!
Pea diseases: Powdery mildew (Sulfur spray), Rust (Mancozeb), Root rot (seed treatment + drainage). Aphids major pest - Imidacloprid!
Pea care: Provide support (sticks/net) for tall varieties, pick pods when plump but green, regular picking encourages more pods. Storage: shell and freeze quickly!
Spinach cultivation: Cool season crop. Sow Sept-Nov (Rabi). Direct sowing in rows 20-25cm apart. Duration 40-50 days for first cutting. Multiple cuttings possible!
Spinach varieties: All Green (Palak), Pusa Jyoti (fast growing), Jobner Green (local), Virginia Savoy (true spinach). Palak is more heat tolerant than true spinach!
Spinach fertilizer: 80-100kg N, 50kg P2O5, 50kg K2O per hectare. Apply nitrogen in 2-3 splits after each cutting. FYM 20 tons/ha!
Spinach care: Keep soil moist, regular cutting encourages growth (cut 2-3 inches above ground), 3-4 cuttings possible, avoid flowering (turns bitter)!
Spinach problems: White rust (avoid overhead irrigation + Metalaxyl), Leaf miner (Spinosad spray), Aphids (Imidacloprid). Organic: neem oil spray!
Carrot cultivation: Cool season root crop. Sow Aug-Nov. Direct sowing (can't transplant). Row spacing 25-30cm. Thin to 5-7cm between plants. Duration 90-120 days!
Carrot varieties: Pusa Kesar (red, Indian), Nantes (orange, European), Pusa Rudhira (dark red), Pusa Yamdagni (red, long), Kuroda (heat tolerant)!
Carrot fertilizer: 50kg N, 50kg P2O5, 50kg K2O per hectare. Light nitrogen - excess causes forked roots. Deep soil preparation essential!
Carrot care: Loose, deep, stone-free soil needed. Thin seedlings at 3-4 leaf stage. Regular irrigation. Hill up soil to cover shoulders (prevents green tops)!
Carrot problems: Forked roots (stones, heavy soil, excess nitrogen), Hairy roots (excess moisture), Cracked roots (irregular irrigation). Prepare soil well!
Radish cultivation: Cool season crop. Sow Sept-Jan (main season). Direct sowing, rows 25-30cm apart. Duration 40-60 days. Fast growing!
Radish varieties: Pusa Chetki (early, 40 days), Japanese White (long, white), Pusa Himani (heat tolerant), Pusa Reshmi (mild pungent), Chinese Pink!
Radish fertilizer: 50kg N, 50kg P2O5, 30kg K2O per hectare. Light nitrogen needed. Deep loose soil for straight roots!
Radish care: Thin seedlings to 5cm apart, regular irrigation (irregular = pithy/cracked roots), harvest on time (overmature = pithy)!
Radish problems: Pithiness (late harvest, hot weather), Forked roots (hard soil), Bolting (long days, heat). Grow in cool season, harvest on time!
Cucumber cultivation: Warm season crop. Sow Feb-March (summer), June-July (Kharif). Spacing 1.5x0.5m. Needs support/trellis. Duration 60-75 days!
Cucumber varieties: Pusa Sanyog (F1, gynoecious), Japanese Long Green, Pant Khira-1, Poinsette, NS-404 (hybrid). Parthenocarpic for greenhouse!
Cucumber fertilizer: 100kg N, 50kg P2O5, 50kg K2O per hectare. Apply nitrogen in 3 splits. FYM 20-25 tons/ha!
Cucumber diseases: Downy mildew (Metalaxyl spray), Powdery mildew (Sulfur), Anthracnose (Mancozeb), Mosaic virus (aphid control + resistant variety)!
Cucumber care: Provide trellis/support, regular picking (harvest daily), pollination important (bees), avoid waterlogging. Pick when dark green, firm!
Bottle gourd cultivation: Warm season vine. Sow Feb-March (summer), June-July (Kharif). Spacing 2.5x1.5m. Needs strong support/pandal. Duration 60-75 days to first harvest!
Lauki varieties: Pusa Naveen (long, 40-45cm), Pusa Summer Prolific Long (cylindrical), Pusa Sandesh (round), Arka Bahar (long), Punjab Long!
Bottle gourd fertilizer: 100kg N, 50kg P2O5, 50kg K2O per hectare. Apply nitrogen in 3 splits. FYM 25-30 tons/ha!
Bottle gourd care: Train on pandal/trellis for straight fruits, hand pollination in morning for better fruit set, regular picking encourages more fruiting!
Bottle gourd problems: Fruit fly (bait traps + Malathion), Powdery mildew (Sulfur), Mosaic virus (aphid control). Pick young, tender fruits!
Bitter gourd cultivation: Warm season vine. Sow Feb-March, June-July. Spacing 2x1.5m. Needs support/trellis. Duration 55-65 days to first harvest!
Karela varieties: Pusa Do Mousami (year-round), Pusa Vishesh (long), Coimbatore Long, Arka Harit (dark green), VNR 28 (hybrid)!
Bitter gourd fertilizer: 80kg N, 60kg P2O5, 60kg K2O per hectare. Apply nitrogen in 3 splits. FYM 20-25 tons/ha!
Bitter gourd care: Train on trellis/pandal, pick when green and firm (before yellowing), regular picking essential, hand pollinate for better yield!
Bitter gourd problems: Fruit fly (most serious - bait traps, early harvest), Powdery mildew (Sulfur), Red pumpkin beetle (Carbaryl). Pick fruits young!
Chickpea cultivation: Rabi pulse crop. Sow Oct-Nov. Seed rate 75-100kg/ha. Spacing 30x10cm. Duration 100-130 days. Rainfed or limited irrigation!
Chickpea varieties: Desi - Pusa 256, JG 11, GNG 1958 (bold). Kabuli - L 550, Pusa 1053 (large seeded, premium price). Choose based on market!
Chickpea fertilizer: 20kg N, 60kg P2O5, 20kg K2O per hectare. Low nitrogen - fixes own. Rhizobium inoculation beneficial!
Chickpea diseases: Wilt (Fusarium - use resistant variety + seed treatment), Ascochyta blight (Mancozeb spray), Pod borer (Helicoverpa - NPV, pheromone traps)!
Chickpea care: One irrigation at pod filling if very dry, avoid excess water (causes wilt), bird scaring at maturity. Harvest when pods turn brown!
Lentil cultivation: Rabi pulse crop. Sow Oct-Nov. Seed rate 40-45kg/ha. Spacing 25-30cm rows. Duration 110-130 days. Mostly rainfed!
Lentil varieties: Pusa Vaibhav (bold seeded), L 4076 (rust resistant), IPL 316 (early), NDL 1 (high yield), K 75 (popular). Small seeded more common!
Lentil fertilizer: 20kg N, 40kg P2O5, 20kg K2O per hectare. Apply at sowing. Rhizobium + PSB inoculation recommended!
Lentil diseases: Rust (most serious - spray Mancozeb when first seen), Wilt (resistant varieties), Collar rot (seed treatment)!
Lentil care: No irrigation usually (rainfed crop), one irrigation at flowering if very dry. Harvest when lower pods turn brown, plants yellowish!
Pigeon pea cultivation: Kharif pulse. Sow June-July. Seed rate 15-20kg/ha. Spacing 60-75cm x 20cm. Duration: Early 150-160 days, Late 200-240 days!
Arhar varieties: Pusa 991 (early, 150 days), Asha (ICPL 87119 - wilt resistant), UPAS 120 (extra early), Maruti (compact). Choose based on duration!
Pigeon pea fertilizer: 20kg N, 50kg P2O5, 20kg K2O per hectare. Low nitrogen needed - fixes own. Apply full at sowing!
Pigeon pea diseases: Wilt (Fusarium - most serious, resistant varieties), Sterility mosaic (SMD - resistant variety + mite control), Pod borer (Helicoverpa - NPV, traps)!
Pigeon pea care: Intercrop with soybean/groundnut, nipping (remove terminal bud at 40-50 days for more branches), bird scaring at maturity. Multiple pickings for green peas!
Mung bean cultivation: Kharif (June-July) and Summer (March-April). Seed rate 20-25kg/ha. Spacing 30x10cm. Duration 60-70 days (short duration)!
Moong varieties: Pusa Vishal (bold seeded), IPM 02-3 (MYMV resistant), SML 668 (high yield), Samrat (early), K 851 (Kharif suitable)!
Mung bean fertilizer: 20kg N, 40-50kg P2O5, 20kg K2O per hectare. Rhizobium + PSB seed treatment beneficial!
Mung bean diseases: Yellow mosaic virus (MYMV - most serious, resistant varieties + whitefly control), Powdery mildew (Sulfur), Cercospora leaf spot (Mancozeb)!
Mung bean care: Short duration crop, 1-2 light irrigations, pick pods as they mature (indeterminate type), thresh when dry!
Citrus cultivation: Plant in monsoon (July-Aug) or Feb-March. Spacing 6x6m. First harvest 4-5 years (budded plants). Long-lived trees (30-50 years)!
Citrus varieties: Nagpur Orange (mandarin), Kinnow (Punjab), Mosambi (sweet lime), Kagzi Nimbu (acid lime), Assam lemon. Choose for your region!
Citrus fertilizer: Per tree per year - 20kg FYM, 600g N, 200g P2O5, 200g K2O (mature tree). Apply in 3 splits (Feb, June, Sept). Micronutrients important!
Citrus diseases: Citrus canker (Copper spray), Gummosis (Copper paste), Greening/HLB (remove infected trees + psylla control), Anthracnose (Carbendazim)!
Citrus care: Basin around tree, mulching, drip irrigation saves water, pruning for shape, pest monitoring (leaf miner, psylla, mites). Bahar treatment for fruiting!
Pomegranate cultivation: Plant in monsoon (July-Aug). Spacing 5x4m. First harvest 3-4 years. Three bahars - Mrig (June-July), Hasta (Sept-Oct), Ambe (Jan-Feb)!
Pomegranate varieties: Bhagwa (red, commercial), Ganesh (pink, soft seeds), Mridula (red), Arakta (dark red). Bhagwa most popular for export!
Pomegranate fertilizer: Per tree - 625g N, 250g P2O5, 250g K2O. Apply in 3 splits. FYM 25kg/tree. Micronutrients spray (Zn, B) important!
Pomegranate diseases: Bacterial blight (most serious - Streptocycline + Copper), Wilt (resistant rootstock), Cercospora (Carbendazim). Fruit cracking - regular irrigation!
Pomegranate care: Bahar treatment (stress + irrigation for flowering), fruit bagging (quality + pest protection), drip irrigation, pruning after harvest!
Grape cultivation: Plant Jan-Feb (rooted cuttings). Spacing 3x2m. Trellis/bower system. First harvest 2-3 years. Pruning critical for yield!
Grape varieties: Thompson Seedless (export, raisin), Sharad Seedless (black), Flame Seedless (red), Sonaka (green), Bangalore Blue (juice, wine)!
Grape fertilizer: Per vine - 500g N, 300g P2O5, 500g K2O. Apply after pruning (Oct), at bud burst (Jan), at fruit development. FYM 25kg/vine!
Grape diseases: Downy mildew (Metalaxyl), Powdery mildew (Sulfur), Anthracnose (Carbendazim). Spray schedule critical - start before monsoon!
Grape care: Pruning most important (Oct-Nov), training system (Y-trellis, bower), gibberellin for berry size, thinning bunches, bagging for quality!
Coconut cultivation: Plant in monsoon (June-Sept). Spacing 7.5x7.5m (175 palms/hectare). First harvest 5-6 years (dwarf), 7-8 years (tall). Lives 80-100 years!
Coconut varieties: West Coast Tall, East Coast Tall, Chowghat Dwarf (Orange/Green), Gangabondam, Hybrid (Tall x Dwarf for early bearing)!
Coconut fertilizer: Per palm per year - 500g N, 320g P2O5, 1200g K2O (adult). Apply in 2 splits (May-June, Sept-Oct). FYM 25kg/palm!
Coconut diseases: Bud rot (Bordeaux paste), Root wilt (Kerala - management only), Leaf rot (Copper spray), Rhinoceros beetle (hook out + naphthalene balls)!
Coconut care: Basin management (4m radius), intercropping (banana, cocoa, pepper), irrigation in summer, husk burial in basin, crown cleaning!
Arecanut cultivation: Plant in monsoon (May-June). Spacing 2.7x2.7m (1360 palms/hectare). First harvest 6-7 years. Shade loving initially!
Arecanut varieties: Mangala, Sumangala, Shreemangala (high yielding), South Kanara (traditional), Mohitnagar. Choose disease-resistant varieties!
Arecanut fertilizer: Per palm - 100g N, 40g P2O5, 140g K2O (adult). Apply in 2 splits. FYM 12kg/palm. Organic matter very important!
Arecanut diseases: Koleroga (fruit rot - Bordeaux spray), Mahali (leaf spot - Copper spray), Yellow leaf disease (management only), Inflorescence dieback!
Arecanut care: Shade management (remove as plants mature), irrigation critical in summer, intercropping (pepper, banana, cocoa), mulching around palms!
Turmeric cultivation: Plant April-May with monsoon onset. Seed rate 2000-2500kg/hectare (finger rhizomes). Spacing 30x15cm. Duration 7-9 months!
Turmeric varieties: Lakadong (high curcumin 7-12%, Meghalaya), Salem (TN), Alleppey (Kerala), Rajapuri (Maharashtra), Prabha, Pratibha (IISR)!
Turmeric fertilizer: 60kg N, 50kg P2O5, 120kg K2O per hectare. Apply nitrogen in 3 splits (planting, 45 days, 90 days). FYM 25-30 tons/ha!
Turmeric diseases: Rhizome rot (Trichoderma + drainage), Leaf blotch (Mancozeb), Shoot borer (Quinalphos). Seed treatment with Trichoderma essential!
Turmeric care: Mulching with dry leaves after planting, earthing up at 60 and 120 days, regular weeding. Harvest when leaves turn yellow and dry!
Ginger cultivation: Plant April-May. Seed rate 1500-1800kg/hectare. Spacing 25x15cm. Shade tolerant (40-50% shade). Duration 8-9 months!
Ginger varieties: Maran, Nadia (West Bengal), Rio de Janeiro, Varada, IISR Mahima (high yield), IISR Rejatha (disease tolerant)!
Ginger fertilizer: 75kg N, 50kg P2O5, 50kg K2O per hectare. Apply nitrogen in 3 splits. FYM 25-30 tons/ha. Mulching critical!
Ginger diseases: Soft rot (most serious - Trichoderma, drainage, seed treatment), Bacterial wilt (resistant seed), Leaf spot (Mancozeb)!
Ginger care: Thick mulching (green leaves) after planting and earthing up, partial shade beneficial, good drainage essential. Harvest for green ginger at 6 months!
Dry chili farming: Varieties - Byadgi (Karnataka, paprika), Guntur Sannam (AP, hot), Teja (hottest), Kashmiri (color, mild). Choose for end use!
Byadgi chili: Famous for deep red color, less pungency. Transplant June-July. Duration 150-180 days. Yield: 15-20q dry/ha. Premium for color!
Guntur Sannam: High pungency, export quality. Spacing 60x45cm. 4-5 pickings. Dry in sun 7-10 days to 10% moisture. 35-40q dry/ha yield!
Chili drying: Sun dry on clean floor for 7-10 days. Final moisture 10%. Avoid rain during drying (causes fungus). Proper drying prevents aflatoxin!
Chili grading: Remove stems, broken pieces, discolored ones. Grade by size, color, and pungency. Store in gunny bags, dry place. Export requires quality certification!
Black pepper cultivation: Plant May-June (monsoon onset). Spacing 3x3m on standards (supporting trees). First harvest 3-4 years. Perennial vine!
Pepper varieties: Panniyur 1 (popular), Karimunda (traditional), IISR Shakti (high yield), Pournami, Sreekara. Quick wilt resistant varieties preferred!
Pepper fertilizer: Per vine - 50g N, 50g P2O5, 150g K2O (adult). Apply in 2 splits (May-June, Sept). FYM 10kg/vine. Mulching essential!
Pepper diseases: Quick wilt (Phytophthora - most serious, Metalaxyl drench), Slow wilt (nematodes - Carbofuran), Pollu (anthracnose - Bordeaux spray)!
Pepper care: Standard trees (Erythrina, Silver oak), trailing and tying, mulching basin, drainage crucial, harvest when one berry turns red on spike!
Seed selection: Buy certified seeds from government agencies, registered dealers, agricultural universities. Check certification tag, lot number, germination percentage!
Certified vs truthfully labeled: Certified (government tested), Truthfully labeled (company responsible). Both acceptable. Avoid market seeds without tags!
Hybrid vs Variety: Hybrids (F1) - higher yield, uniformity, costly, can't save seeds. Varieties/OPV - lower cost, can save seeds, less uniform. Choose based on need!
Quality indicators: Germination 80%+ for most crops, physical purity 98%+, moisture content proper, free from weeds and other crop seeds, healthy appearance!
Seed sources: State Seed Corporations, NSC, Private companies (certified), KVK, Agricultural universities, Registered dealers. Keep purchase receipt!
Land preparation steps: 1) Remove previous crop residue, 2) Deep plowing (summer), 3) 2-3 harrowings, 4) Planking/leveling, 5) Layout beds/channels!
Summer plowing benefits: Kills pests, weeds, diseases. Exposes soil to sun. Improves water infiltration. Do 1 deep plowing in May-June!
Tillage operations: Primary (moldboard plow, disc plow - deep), Secondary (cultivator, harrow - pulverize), Leveling (planker, laser leveler)!
Seedbed for direct sowing: Fine tilth for small seeds (carrot, onion), coarse for large seeds (maize, groundnut). Remove clods and debris!
Transplanting preparation: Incorporate FYM/compost 2-3 weeks before, prepare beds/ridges, ensure good drainage. Apply basal fertilizer!
Sowing methods: Broadcasting (scatter), Line sowing (rows), Dibbling (holes), Drilling (continuous line), Transplanting (seedlings). Choose based on crop!
Broadcasting: Scatter seeds uniformly. Used for rice (wet), wheat (sometimes). More seed needed, uneven spacing, difficult weeding!
Line sowing: Using seed drill or marking lines. Uniform spacing, easy weeding, less seed. Best for wheat, pulses, oilseeds!
Transplanting: Raise nursery, transplant seedlings. Used for rice, vegetables, some crops. Better establishment, uniform crop!
Sowing depth: General rule - 2-3 times seed diameter. Small seeds (carrot) - shallow. Large seeds (maize) - deeper. Firm soil after sowing!
Common crop spacing: Rice (20x15cm), Wheat (20-22cm rows), Tomato (60x45cm), Potato (60x20cm), Onion (15x10cm), Cotton (90x60cm), Sugarcane (90cm rows)!
Vegetables spacing: Tomato (60x45cm), Brinjal (60x45cm), Chili (60x45cm), Cabbage (45x45cm), Okra (45x30cm), Cucumber (1.5x0.5m)!
Fruits spacing: Mango (10x10m), Banana (1.8x1.8m), Papaya (2x2m), Guava (6x6m), Pomegranate (5x4m), Citrus (6x6m)!
Why spacing matters: Proper light interception, air circulation (disease reduction), nutrient/water access, easy operations, optimal yield!
Plants per hectare: Calculate = 10000 ÷ (row spacing in m × plant spacing in m). Example: Tomato 60x45cm = 10000 ÷ (0.6x0.45) = 37,037 plants/ha!
Critical irrigation stages: Rice (transplanting, tillering, flowering), Wheat (CRI, flowering, grain filling), Pulses (flowering, pod development)!
Water requirement: Rice (1200-1500mm), Wheat (400-450mm), Sugarcane (1800-2200mm), Cotton (700-1200mm), Vegetables (400-600mm per crop)!
Irrigation scheduling: Observe soil (dry 2-3 inches = irrigate), plant (wilting = urgent), or use IW/CPE ratio (Irrigation Water / Cumulative Pan Evaporation)!
Over-watering signs: Yellowing, wilting despite wet soil, root rot, fungal diseases. Under-watering: wilting, leaf curl, slow growth, flower/fruit drop!
Water saving: Drip/sprinkler, mulching, rainwater harvesting, deficit irrigation (critical stages only), short duration varieties!
Kharif season (June-Oct): Rice, Maize, Sorghum, Pearl millet, Cotton, Soybean, Groundnut, Pigeon pea, Mung bean, Sesame. Plant with monsoon onset!
Rabi season (Oct-March): Wheat, Barley, Mustard, Chickpea, Lentil, Peas, Potato, Onion, Garlic. Plant after monsoon withdrawal!
Zaid/Summer (March-June): Watermelon, Muskmelon, Cucumber, Bottle gourd, Summer moong, Sunflower, Vegetables. Need irrigation!
Vegetables calendar: Year-round (tomato, brinjal, okra with variety choice), Winter (peas, cabbage, cauliflower), Summer (cucurbits, leafy greens)!
Fruits calendar: Mango (harvest April-June), Banana (year-round planting), Citrus (harvest Nov-Feb), Grape (harvest Feb-April)!
Yield improvement basics: Right variety, quality seeds, timely sowing, optimal spacing, balanced fertilization, water management, pest/disease control!
Variety selection: Choose high-yielding, disease-resistant varieties suited for your region. Use certified seeds. 20-30% yield difference possible!
Fertilizer management: Based on soil test. Balanced NPK, micronutrients, split application of nitrogen. Organic + inorganic combination works best!
Plant protection: Regular monitoring, timely action, IPM approach. Prevent rather than cure. 10-30% yield saved through proper pest management!
Technology adoption: Drip irrigation, mulching, raised beds, precision farming, mechanization. Combine traditional wisdom with modern techniques!

Rice climate: 20-37°C temperature, 100-200cm annual rainfall, high humidity. Grows well in tropical and subtropical regions with flooded conditions!
Wheat climate: 15-25°C during growth, 10-15°C at tillering, cool weather crop. Rainfall 50-75cm. Rabi season ideal. Can't tolerate waterlogging!
Tomato climate: 20-27°C optimal, can't tolerate frost. Needs moderate rainfall. Too much humidity causes diseases. Day-night temperature difference improves fruiting!
Mango climate: Tropical/subtropical, 24-30°C ideal. Needs dry period for flowering (Nov-Feb), monsoon for fruit development. Can't tolerate frost or prolonged cold!
Cotton climate: Warm weather crop, 21-30°C optimal. Needs 50-100cm rainfall, sunny days, frost-free period 180-200 days. Excessive rain during boll opening harmful!
Rice: Heavy clay loam, good water retention. pH 5.5-6.5. Can grow in poorly drained soils (actually prefers flooded!). Black cotton soil, alluvial soil excellent!
Wheat: Well-drained loamy soil, pH 6.0-7.5. Can tolerate slight alkalinity. Deep soil preferred. Black soil, alluvial, and loam all suitable!
Groundnut: Light sandy loam to loam, well-drained. pH 6.0-6.5. Loose soil needed for pod development. Red soil, laterite soil good. Avoid heavy clay!
Cotton: Deep black cotton soil (vertisol) ideal. Also grows in alluvial, red loam. pH 6.5-8.0. Good moisture retention needed. Avoid waterlogging!
Vegetables: Most prefer loamy soil with good drainage and organic matter. pH 6.0-7.0. Sandy loam for root crops (carrot, radish). Clay loam for leafy vegetables!
Kharif season (Monsoon): June-October. Crops: Rice, Maize, Cotton, Soybean, Groundnut, Jowar, Bajra. Plant with monsoon onset, harvest Oct-Nov!
Rabi season (Winter): October-March. Crops: Wheat, Mustard, Chickpea, Peas, Barley. Sow after monsoon, harvest Feb-April. Needs irrigation!
Zaid/Summer: March-June. Crops: Watermelon, Muskmelon, Cucumber, Moong (summer), Sunflower. Short duration, needs irrigation!
Year-round crops: Banana, Papaya can be planted any time with irrigation. Vegetables like Tomato, Brinjal have varieties for all seasons!
Perennial crops: Mango, Coconut, Sugarcane, Fruit trees - plant during monsoon (July-Aug) for best establishment. Can also plant in Feb-March with irrigation!
Rice: 30-40kg seed/hectare for nursery (transplanting), 80-100kg for direct seeding. Hybrid rice needs 15-20kg/ha!
Wheat: 100kg/hectare for timely sowing (Nov 1-15), 125kg for late sowing. Use higher for broadcasting, lower for line sowing!
Maize: 20-25kg/hectare for hybrids, 18-20kg for composites. Lower seed rate but larger seeds. Spacing matters more!
Pulses: Chickpea (75-100kg/ha), Pigeon pea (15-20kg/ha), Moong (20-25kg/ha), Lentil (40-45kg/ha). Varies by seed size!
Vegetables: Tomato (200-250g/ha for nursery), Onion (8-10kg/ha direct), Chili (1-1.5kg/ha for nursery). Most vegetables need nursery first!
Short duration (60-90 days): Moong bean (60-70), Radish (40-60), Spinach (40-50), Muskmelon (70-80). Quick returns, multiple cropping possible!
Medium duration (90-150 days): Wheat (120-140), Rice (120-150), Tomato (90-120), Chickpea (100-130), Maize (90-120). Most common crops!
Long duration (150-300 days): Cotton (150-180), Sugarcane (300-360), Pigeon pea late varieties (200-240), Turmeric (240-270). Need patient investment!
Fruit crops: Papaya (9-10 months to first fruit), Banana (11-13 months), Mango (3-5 years for grafted), Guava (3-4 years). Perennials give for many years!
Duration varies by variety: Early, mid, late varieties available for most crops. Choose based on your market timing and rotation needs!
Cereal + Pulse intercropping: Maize + Soybean, Maize + Cowpea, Sorghum + Pigeon pea. Legumes fix nitrogen, improve soil fertility!
Cash crop intercropping: Cotton + Groundnut, Sugarcane + Potato (early), Sugarcane + Onion, Coconut + Banana + Pepper (multilayer)!
Vegetable intercropping: Tomato + Onion, Cabbage + Lettuce, Okra + Cowpea. Different heights and root depths utilize space better!
Benefits: Better land use, risk reduction, improved soil health, pest management, additional income. One crop compensates if other fails!
Precautions: Choose compatible crops, avoid competition for same resources, different maturity periods better, maintain proper spacing for both crops!
High rainfall crops (150-250cm): Rice (150-200cm), Jute (150-200cm), Sugarcane (180-220cm), Banana (150-180cm). Need good water availability!
Medium rainfall crops (75-150cm): Cotton (75-100cm), Maize (60-100cm), Groundnut (50-75cm), Sorghum (40-65cm). Moderate water needs!
Low rainfall crops (30-75cm): Bajra (40-60cm), Gram/Chickpea (60-90cm), Mustard (40-50cm). Drought tolerant, good for rainfed areas!
Rain distribution matters: Well-distributed rain better than total amount. Rice needs water throughout, Wheat needs early moisture, Cotton needs rain during vegetative stage!
Rainfed vs Irrigated: Rainfed farming depends entirely on monsoon. Irrigated farming gives flexibility, multiple crops, better yields. Choose crops matching rainfall!
Frost damage symptoms: Water-soaked appearance, wilting, browning of leaves, blackening of tender parts. Damaged tissue can't recover!
Prevention methods: Light irrigation evening before frost (wet soil holds heat), smoke/fires upwind of field, cover crops with straw/cloth, avoid low-lying areas!
Timing: Frost risk in North India Dec-Jan. Monitor weather forecasts. Critical for vegetables, fruit trees during flowering!
Crop selection: Frost-tolerant crops - wheat, peas, mustard, cabbage. Sensitive - rice, cotton, tomato, banana, mango flowers. Choose accordingly!
Recovery: Don't remove damaged parts immediately, wait for new growth. Light irrigation, foliar nutrition help recovery. Severe frost may need replanting!
Heat stress symptoms: Leaf curling, wilting midday, leaf burn edges, flower/fruit drop, reduced growth. Yields drop significantly!
Management: Frequent light irrigation (cooling), mulching (soil temperature down), shade nets (vegetables), spray water on leaves (evaporative cooling)!
Critical stages: Flowering and grain filling most sensitive. Heat during wheat grain filling reduces yield. Protect during these stages!
Heat-tolerant crops: Sorghum, Bajra, Watermelon, Cucumber, Okra suited for hot weather. Choose varieties with heat tolerance!
Prevention: Plant early to avoid peak summer, use mulch, drip irrigation (saves water + cools), grow windbreaks, select heat-tolerant varieties!
Drought-tolerant crops: Bajra, Jowar, Gram, Moth bean, Cluster bean, Castor. Choose for low rainfall areas (<50cm annual)!
Water conservation: Drip irrigation (70% water saving), mulching, rainwater harvesting, farm ponds, percolation tanks. Every drop counts!
Agronomic practices: Deep plowing (moisture retention), timely sowing, wider spacing (less competition), remove weeds (water thieves), use anti-transpirants!
Variety selection: Short duration varieties escape terminal drought. Drought-tolerant varieties withstand stress. Seed companies provide specific varieties!
Contingency planning: Keep alternative short-duration crops ready, crop insurance, diversify crops, maintain livestock for backup income!
Waterlogging effects: Root rot, oxygen deficiency, yellowing, wilting despite wet soil, stunted growth, fungal diseases. Kills most crops except rice!
Immediate action: Drain water ASAP through channels, pumping. Make drainage channels along field boundaries. Time is critical!
Prevention: Raised bed planting (vegetables), deep plowing (breaks hard pan), avoid over-irrigation, improve soil structure (organic matter), install subsurface drainage!
Crop selection: Rice thrives in waterlogged conditions. Jute tolerates waterlogging. Most other crops need good drainage!
Post-waterlogging: Light cultivation after water drains, foliar spray micronutrients (roots damaged), pest/disease monitoring (weakened plants susceptible)!
Hill farming advantages: Cooler climate suits temperate crops, organic farming easier, premium quality produce, multiple elevation zones for different crops!
Suitable crops: Apple, Pear, Plum (high hills), Potato, Cabbage, Cauliflower (mid-hills), Ginger, Turmeric, Cardamom (lower hills), Medicinal plants!
Challenges: Soil erosion (heavy rain), transport difficulty, smaller land holdings, limited mechanization, wild animal damage. Need specific solutions!
Terrace farming: Reduces soil erosion, conserves moisture, creates level planting surface. Labor-intensive but essential for slopes. Traditional wisdom works!
Soil conservation: Contour farming, stone bunds, terracing, mulching, cover crops, agroforestry. Plant grass strips along slopes. Prevent erosion at all costs!
Coastal challenges: Soil salinity, saline groundwater, salt spray, cyclones, high humidity, sandy soil. Need special crop and management choices!
Salt-tolerant crops: Coconut (highly tolerant), Date palm, Beet, Asparagus, Barley (moderate), Palmarosa, Casuarina. Check salinity tolerance levels!
Coconut farming: Ideal for coastal areas. Plant 7.5x7.5m spacing. Needs good drainage. Tolerates salt spray. Intercrop with banana, pineapple!
Salinity management: Leaching (flush salts), drainage, organic matter addition, gypsum application, choose tolerant crops/varieties. Don't fight nature!
Alternative: Aquaculture integration (shrimp/fish farming), mangrove restoration, salt production. Utilize coastal advantages!
Monsoon/Kharif season: June to October. Southwest monsoon brings rain. Major farming season in India. 50%+ crops grown in this season!
Main Kharif crops: Rice (most important), Maize, Cotton, Soybean, Groundnut, Jowar, Bajra, Moong, Urad, Arhar. Plant with monsoon onset!
Timing crucial: Early sowing (with first good rain) gives better yields. Delayed sowing reduces yields significantly. Monitor rainfall forecasts!
Disease management critical: High humidity promotes fungal diseases. Need preventive sprays. Good drainage essential. Monitor crops regularly!
Monsoon advantages: Natural irrigation (reduces cost), soil moisture for germination, suitable for rainfed crops, lower temperature than summer!
Rabi/Winter season: October to March. Sow after monsoon withdrawal. Harvest Feb-April. Second major cropping season!
Main Rabi crops: Wheat (most important), Mustard, Gram/Chickpea, Peas, Lentil, Barley, Potato, Onion, Garlic. Need irrigation!
Advantages: Lower pest pressure, cool weather suits temperate crops, good grain quality (wheat), higher market prices for vegetables!
Irrigation essential: Most Rabi crops need 4-6 irrigations. Ensure water availability before sowing. Wheat needs irrigation at critical stages!
Frost risk: Watch forecasts in North India (Dec-Jan). Protect vegetables and wheat at flowering. Some crops damaged by severe frost!
Zaid/Summer season: March to June. Short season between Rabi and Kharif. Needs assured irrigation. Hot weather farming!
Main Zaid crops: Watermelon, Muskmelon, Cucumber, Bottle gourd, Bitter gourd, Moong (summer), Sunflower, Fodder crops!
Advantages: Less disease pressure, better market prices (off-season), quick returns (short duration), utilize post-Rabi period!
Challenges: High temperature stress, water requirement high, limited crop choices. Need heat-tolerant varieties!
Water management critical: Drip irrigation best (saves water). Mulching reduces evaporation. Frequent light irrigation better than heavy occasional!
Vegetables year-round: Tomato (varieties for all seasons), Brinjal, Okra, Leafy greens (different types), Chili, Coriander. Variety selection key!
Perennial crops: Banana, Papaya, Sugarcane, Drumstick, Curry leaf, Fruit trees (mango, guava, citrus). Plant once, harvest for years!
Protected cultivation: Polyhouse allows growing vegetables year-round despite external climate. Temperature and pest control. Higher investment!
Hydroponics/Soilless: Grow lettuce, herbs, tomatoes year-round indoors. Controlled environment. No seasonal dependency!
Continuous planting: Succession planting vegetables every 2-4 weeks ensures continuous harvest. Good for leafy vegetables, beans, radish!
Major tropical crops: Rice, Coconut, Banana, Rubber, Cocoa, Coffee, Tea, Spices (pepper, cardamom, turmeric), Cashew, Arecanut!
Climate characteristics: High temperature year-round (25-35°C), high rainfall (150-300cm), high humidity, no frost. Ideal for specific crops!
Coconut farming: 7.5x7.5m spacing, 175 palms/hectare. First harvest 5-6 years. Intercrop with banana, pineapple, cocoa. Lives 80-100 years!
Spice cultivation: Black pepper (vine, needs support tree), Cardamom (shade loving), Turmeric, Ginger (monsoon planting). High value crops!
Challenges: Pest pressure high (warm humid), disease management critical, need good drainage despite high rainfall, cyclone risk in coastal areas!
Temperate fruits: Apple, Pear, Plum, Apricot, Cherry, Peach, Walnut, Almond. Need chilling hours (cold winter) for proper fruiting!
Temperate vegetables: Cabbage, Cauliflower, Broccoli, Lettuce, Spinach, Peas, Carrot, Turnip. Prefer cool growing conditions!
Chilling requirement: Apple needs 1200-1500 chilling hours below 7°C. Varieties differ. Critical for fruit set. Why apples don't fruit in plains!
Growing regions: Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Kashmir, Nilgiris for temperate fruits. High hills (1500-3000m elevation) ideal!
Advantages: Less pest pressure, premium quality fruit, good storage life, high market value. Disadvantages: Transport cost, limited season, hail damage risk!
Dryland/Semi-arid crops: Bajra, Jowar, Gram, Moth bean, Cluster bean, Groundnut, Castor, Sesame. Annual rainfall 30-75cm!
Key practices: Moisture conservation (deep plowing, mulching), rainwater harvesting, drought-tolerant varieties, wider spacing, timely operations!
Soil management: Increase organic matter (water holding), reduce tillage, form bunds (prevent runoff), contour farming on slopes!
Contingency crops: Keep short-duration backup crops. If main crop fails due to drought, plant quick-maturing alternative (moong, cluster bean)!
Livestock integration: Mixed farming - crops + animals. Animals provide insurance during crop failure. Drought-tolerant animals (goats, sheep)!

Organic certification process: 1) Choose certification agency (Ecocert, OneCert, Control Union, etc.), 2) Apply with land details, 3) Conversion period 2-3 years, 4) Inspections, 5) Certificate issued!
Requirements: No synthetic chemicals for 3 years, maintain records (inputs, operations, sales), follow organic standards, allow inspections, buffer zone from conventional farms!
Certification agencies: Accredited by APEDA under NPOP (National Program for Organic Production). List available at apeda.gov.in. Choose nearby agency!
Cost: Rs.15,000-50,000 depending on area and agency. Annual renewal. Group certification cheaper (farmers organize into groups). Some government subsidies available!
Benefits: Premium price 20-50% higher, export opportunities, assured market through organic stores, healthier farming, government support schemes!
Crop rotation benefits: Breaks pest/disease cycles, improves soil fertility, reduces weed pressure, balances nutrient use, better yields, risk management!
Pest/disease management: Same crop continuously builds up specific pests and diseases. Rotation breaks the cycle. Example: rotating away from tomato reduces wilt!
Soil fertility: Legumes (gram, moong) fix nitrogen for next crop. Deep-rooted crops bring up nutrients. Rotation prevents nutrient depletion!
Good rotations: Rice-Wheat (most common), Cotton-Wheat, Maize-Mustard, Rice-Gram, Sugarcane-Wheat-Moong. Include legumes for nitrogen!
Avoid continuous: Monocropping (same crop every season) depletes specific nutrients, builds pests, reduces yields over time. Always rotate!
Fallow period: Leaving land uncropped for a season. Allows soil to rest, replenish nutrients, moisture conservation, breaks pest/disease cycles!
Summer fallow: Leave land empty May-June after Rabi harvest. Deep plowing exposes pests/diseases to sun. Conserves monsoon moisture for Kharif!
Benefits: Improves soil structure, increases organic matter decomposition, moisture storage, pest reduction, allows repair of soil health!
Modern alternative: Instead of complete fallow, grow green manure crops (dhaincha, sunhemp) and incorporate before flowering. Adds organic matter + nitrogen!
When to fallow: Severely degraded land, buildup of serious diseases, need moisture conservation. Otherwise, productive use with green manure better!
Organic mulches: Paddy straw (cheap, widely used), sugarcane trash, dry leaves, grass clippings, wood chips, coconut coir, FYM. Decompose and add nutrients!
Plastic mulch: Black (weed control + heat), Silver (pest repellent + heat reflection), White (cool season), Transparent (soil solarization). Durable, effective!
Living mulch: Cover crops between main crops (clover between fruit trees). Suppress weeds, add nitrogen, continuous soil cover!
Stone/gravel mulch: Permanent, good for orchards, low maintenance. Doesn't add nutrients but conserves moisture, controls temperature!
Selection criteria: Cost, availability, crop type, purpose (weed/moisture/temperature), decomposition rate. Combine types for best results!
Green manure: Growing specific crops and incorporating into soil before flowering. Adds organic matter, nitrogen (if legume), improves soil structure!
Best green manure crops: Dhaincha/Sesbania (50kg seed/ha, 45 days), Sunhemp (25kg seed/ha, 50 days), Cowpea (30kg/ha, 45 days), Cluster bean, Moong!
Process: Sow before monsoon (May-June), grow 45-60 days, incorporate at flowering stage by plowing/rotavator. Wait 2 weeks before main crop planting!
Benefits: Adds 60-80kg N/ha (legumes), 15-20 tons organic matter/ha, improves water holding capacity, suppresses weeds, breaks pest cycles!
Best for rice: Grow dhaincha before rice transplanting. Sow in May, incorporate in June after first good rain, transplant rice 2 weeks later. Saves nitrogen fertilizer!
Precision farming: Using technology (GPS, sensors, drones, data analytics) for site-specific crop management. Right input, right amount, right place, right time!
Technologies: GPS-guided tractors (straight rows, overlap reduction), Soil sensors (moisture, nutrients), Drones (monitoring, spraying), Variable rate fertilizer applicators!
Benefits: Reduces input cost (20-30%), increases yield (10-15%), environmental friendly, saves water, precise application, data-driven decisions!
Affordable options: Smartphone apps (weather, market prices, advisory), soil testing, drip irrigation with timer, simple moisture sensors. Start small!
Future farming: AI-powered pest detection, automated irrigation, harvest robots, satellite monitoring. Gradually becoming affordable for small farmers through cooperatives!
Climate-smart agriculture: Farming that sustainably increases productivity, builds resilience to climate change, reduces greenhouse emissions!
Practices: Crop diversification, drought/flood tolerant varieties, rainwater harvesting, conservation agriculture, agroforestry, renewable energy use!
